abstract: Upwork's In-Demand Skills 2026 report (published February 4, 2026) analyzes actual completed-job freelancer earnings across six categories in 2025. Top AI-applied skills grew 109% year-over-year, with AI video generation +329%, AI integration +178%, and AI data annotation +154%. Traditional categories (full-stack dev, virtual assistance, data analytics, graphic design) stayed consistently strong. Nearly half of business leaders say they would pay a premium for creative, innovative independent talent — a bifurcation signal for freelancer rates.
keyFindings: Top AI-applied freelance skills grew 109% year-over-year in 2025
AI image generation/editing skills: +95% YoY; AI chatbot development +71% YoY
Traditional skills (full-stack development, virtual assistance, data analytics, graphic design) remained consistently strong
Nearly 50% of business leaders say they'd pay a premium for creative, innovative independent talent
Human-AI collaboration boosts project completion by up to 70%, even on simple tasks
methodology: Analysis of completed-job freelancer earnings on the Upwork Marketplace from January 1 to December 31, 2025 (US-based demand). Minimum $100,000 in aggregate freelancer earnings per skill required for inclusion. Six work categories covered. Not survey- or posting-based — reflects actual client spend.
qualifiers: Upwork is a Tier 1 corporate data source (earnings-derived) but has a commercial interest in framing the marketplace positively. Report emphasizes growth categories more than declining ones — writing and translation category-level rate declines are not disclosed in this release. Growth percentages are on spend by skill, not average freelancer hourly rates directly.
